# BlueTusk

> BlueTusk is a PostgreSQL-native platform for .NET covering ADO.NET, EF Core, replication, real-time delivery, extensions, and graph workloads.

Use this index to find the canonical HTML documentation. The complete curated guide set is available at [llms-full.txt](https://bluetusk.io/llms-full.txt).

## Start here

- [BlueTusk overview](https://bluetusk.io/)
- [Quickstart](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/quickstart)
- [Installation](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/install)
- [Documentation hub](https://bluetusk.io/documentation)
- [Release evidence](https://bluetusk.io/evidence)

## Getting started

- [Install BlueTusk](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/install): Choose the stable or RC channel, install the smallest NuGet/npm package set, pin exact versions, and verify the resolved dependency graph.
- [Quickstart: run the first query](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/quickstart): Create a .NET console app, install BlueTusk, run a parameterized PostgreSQL query, and understand data-source ownership.
- [Core concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/concepts): Learn data-source ownership, sessions, capabilities, type identity, checkpoints, source identity, and release-state vocabulary.
- [Architecture](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/architecture): Understand the layers, dependency direction, ownership, and async boundaries.
- [ADO.NET](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/provider-overview): Connect a .NET application, run safe SQL, and choose the right command, transaction, batch, or bulk API.

## Provider

- [Authentication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/authentication): Credentials, password files, TLS certificates, GSSAPI, Kerberos, and SSPI.
- [Cloud identity](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/cloud-identity): AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud identity integration and live-test boundaries.
- [Dependency injection and health checks](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/dependency-injection): Register one long-lived provider data source, consume DbDataSource, and design readiness checks without harming liveness.
- [Connection pooling](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pooling): Pool sizing, reset behavior, operational signals, and PgBouncer modes.
- [Multi-host connections](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/multi-host): Multi-host routing, failover, target session attributes, and recovery.
- [Batches](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/batches): Execute ordered command batches with PostgreSQL-aware error behavior.
- [COPY](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/copy): Text and binary COPY APIs, typed values, cancellation, and completion.
- [Large objects](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/large-objects): Large-object ownership and streaming behavior.
- [Asynchronous notifications](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/notifications): LISTEN and NOTIFY lifecycle, dispatch, and connection behavior.
- [Sequential readers](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/sequential-readers): Bounded sequential reads for large PostgreSQL values.
- [Schema discovery](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/schema-discovery): Use GetSchema, GetColumnSchema, GetSchemaTable, restrictions, and provider-neutral catalogue metadata.
- [Use PostgreSQL types](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/types): Read and write common, custom, array, JSON, temporal, and extension-defined PostgreSQL values from .NET.
- [PostgreSQL 19 native REPACK](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/repack): Run and monitor PostgreSQL 19 native REPACK safely from .NET.
- [PostgreSQL pipeline mode](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pipeline-mode): Pipeline groups, protocol Sync boundaries, and ordered failures.
- [Start PostgreSQL replication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/replication): Open a dedicated replication session, decode pgoutput, and acknowledge only durable transaction progress.

## EF Core

- [Use BlueTusk with Entity Framework Core](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/overview): Set up an EF Core context, query and save data, create migrations, and prepare the provider for production.

## Real time

- [BlueTusk real-time platform](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/platform): Choose Streams, Sync, Live, Continuous Graph, or Control Plane from the outcome your application needs.
- [Delivery guarantees in plain language](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/contracts): Understand when work is durable, when it may be replayed, and what each real-time product guarantees.
- [BlueTusk Streams](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams): Turn PostgreSQL changes into complete transactions with bounded storage, durable progress, and safe recovery.
- [Consistent snapshot bootstrap](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/snapshot-bootstrap): A fenced snapshot-then-stream protocol.
- [PostgreSQL durable relay](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/durable-relay): Storage, backup, groups, retention, and relay fan-out.
- [Streams checkpoint and lease stores](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/state-stores): State-store contracts and supported persistence behavior.
- [Hosting and observability](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-hosting): Hosted services, health checks, metrics, and operational behavior.
- [Keep another system in sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync): Keep PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch, NATS, Kafka, S3, or a webhook current from committed changes.
- [Push live updates to applications](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live): Register one authorized query and keep browser or .NET clients updated with bounded, resumable changes.
- [Operate BlueTusk from the dashboard](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane): Run the dashboard, inspect every product, drill into unhealthy resources, and authorize audited operations.
- [Real-time operations](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/operations): Operate source identity, checkpoints, relay storage, destinations, failover, reconciliation, rebuilds, and endurance evidence.
- [Keep graph query results current](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/continuous-graph): Keep a bounded SQL/PGQ result current with incremental updates and authoritative repair.

## Extensions

- [Use PostgreSQL extensions](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/extensions/catalog): Choose and configure typed support for PostGIS, pgvector, TimescaleDB, citext, and other extensions.

## Graph

- [Query a PostgreSQL property graph](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/sql-pgq): Define a PostgreSQL property graph, run a safe GRAPH_TABLE query, and inspect or map it from .NET.

## Operations

- [Production checklist](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/production-checklist): Take a BlueTusk application from package selection to a secure, bounded, observable, recoverable, and operator-owned production deployment.
- [Deployment and configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/deployment): Design production topology, security roles, pool capacity, migrations, rolling deployment, and real-time persistence.
- [Diagnostics and observability](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/observability): Metrics, traces, and slow-command events.
- [Troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/troubleshooting): Diagnose connection, TLS, authentication, pool, command, type, EF, replication, and destination failures from the lowest boundary upward.
- [Security review](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/security): Apply secure connection, identity, secret-handling, and diagnostics defaults before production.
- [Performance engineering](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/performance): Measure pool pressure, command paths, multiplexing, allocation, readers, COPY, and real-time throughput with reproducible evidence.
- [Upgrade guide](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/upgrade-guide): Upgrade product families, EF Core, extensions, PostgreSQL, formats, mappings, and rolling deployments with a recoverable plan.
